I understand that 5 was chosen so as to incentivize quicker packing in of attestations. But I wonder if it introduces a disincentive here too with the shorter bound here. I have asked before several times in the eth2 channel why this was chosen this way instead of the opposite (put stronger conditions on the target instead of source) and never got an answer The only explanation I could think was "to not give source for free" Ah k, do you have a link to the convo ? Also puts validators attesting at epoch transitions at a bigger risk. Now instead of losing the target reward, you lose everything and end up being penalised. Had a question on the modified `Process_Attestations` in Altair. 
https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/specs/altair/beacon-chain.md#modified-process_attestation
```py
    if is_matching_source and state.slot <= data.slot + integer_squareroot(SLOTS_PER_EPOCH):
        participation_flag_indices.append(TIMELY_SOURCE_FLAG_INDEX)
```
With `SLOTS_PER_EPOCH` being 32 , `integer_squareroot(SLOTS_PER_EPOCH)` being 5, this gives a much shorter timeframe to get attestations with a matching source included. I understand that 5 was chosen so as to incentivize quicker packing in of attestations. But I wonder if it introduces a disincentive here too with the shorter bound here. In the event there is any chain instability all attestations with a different target will be thrown away if they cant make into the provided timeframe of 5 slots.

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Why will they be thrown away? you can have `TIMELY_TARGET_FLAG_INDEX` and not `TIMELY_SOURCE_FLAG_INDEX` as they are now independent
